# #3699: Patch: follow-up to #3682 from the after-merge spot-check
Opened by @jgoetzmann-bot.

<!-- jackioh-bot:spot-check-follow-up #3682 -->
The after-merge spot-check of #3682 ([run](https://github.com/Jlore-Studios/JackiOh/actions/runs/42973450742)) found 1 blocking problem(s) in the change as it merged (`3a3de664a2af`). `claude-1` (claude, `opus`, strong) reviewed it. #3682 stays merged: nothing is reverted, and this issue fixes what it found in a change of its own, from `main`.

## What to fix

- [ ] `apps/web/src/net/first-load.test.ts:91`: Since #3682, the #3499 test 'no built script, a worker's included, holds patch-meta.ts's disk reader' can no longer fail: a Vite bundle without `patchMeta()` now resolves `#jackioh-patch-meta` to `patch-meta.browser.ts`, which statically imports the whole 650 KB `patches.json`, and the test's probe string is not in that file, so the bloat it guards against now ships with every test green.
  Evidence: The test treats a bundle as a regression only if it contains the literal "holds an entry with no version" (first-load.test.ts:97). Before #3682, a bundle without the plugin (the practice worker's own plugin list, vite.config.ts:57) fell through to `patch-meta.ts`, whose code carries that string, so the test caught it. After #3682, apps/web/package.json maps the `browser` condition to `patch-meta.browser.ts`. Vite's client and worker resolution applies the `browser` condition, so such a bundle now gets the browser file instead. Its error strings are "is not a list of patches", "holds a patch with no version string" and "holds no patches". The PR says it chose them on purpose to keep the probe 'specific to patch-meta.ts'. Its own new comment in vite.config.ts:56 says that without `patchMeta()` the worker would bundle the 650 KB history. The other #3499 guards miss this: the probe-text and gzip tests read only the entry chunk and its preloads (`entryAndPreloads()`), which leaves out worker chunks, and the 'no static import of patches.json' test scans only `src/`, while the browser file sits at the package root. Fix: make the worker test also flag any built script holding a marker that only the browser file carries, such as its "holds a patch with no version string" error, and update the test's comment to name both files.

## Done when

- Each finding above is fixed where it points, or answered with the evidence that it does not hold.
- Every check is green, with no test skipped, ignored or weakened to get there (CLAUDE.md rule 12).

---
Opened by @jgoetzmann-bot from the after-merge spot-check (one in 5 medium or hard merges, `spot_check_every`): `muse` (`muse`) built #3682 and `muse` (`muse-spark-1.3-contributor`) approved it. This issue's own pull request is never spot-checked.

<!-- jackioh-bot -->

_Written by `muse` (muse, `muse-spark-1.3-contributor`, medium) ([run](https://github.com/Jlore-Studios/JackiOh/actions/runs/42976181685)) before anyone built this. The night bot's builder starts from this section: edit it here to change the plan._

## Goal

Fix the #3499 worker-bloat guard in `apps/web/src/net/first-load.test.ts` so it fails again when a built worker script bundles the patch history. The test at line 91 must flag a built script holding either the disk reader's marker or the browser file's marker, and its comment must name both source files. Nothing about #3682 is reverted.

## Files to touch

| File | Mode | Change |
|---|---|---|
| apps/web/src/net/first-load.test.ts | change | Worker test probes both markers |

Do not touch `apps/web/patch-meta.ts`, `apps/web/patch-meta.browser.ts`, `apps/web/package.json`, `apps/web/vite.config.ts`, any crate, or any other app. No spec section changes and no new ruling note: this is a test repair, not a rules decision the spec leaves open (context only: SPEC §5.1, the two patch-history facts; CLAUDE.md rule 7, client renders only).

## Steps

1. In `apps/web/src/net/first-load.test.ts`, open the `it("#3499 no built script, a worker's included, holds patch-meta.ts's disk reader", ...)` test (lines 91–99). Rename its title to name both files, e.g. `it("#3499 no built script, a worker's included, holds patch-meta.ts's disk reader or patch-meta.browser.ts's bundle", ...)`.
2. In the same test, replace the comment (lines 92–93) with one naming both files and both markers, e.g. that a bundle lacking `patchMeta()` takes `patch-meta.ts` (whose code carries `holds an entry with no version`) or, under the `browser` condition from `package.json`'s `imports`, `patch-meta.browser.ts` (whose code carries `holds a patch with no version string` and statically imports the 650 KB history).
3. In the same test, replace the single-probe filter on line 97 with a two-probe filter. Copy this pattern, keeping both literal spellings exact:
```ts
const readers = scripts.filter((name) => {
  const text = readFileSync(join(assets, name), "utf8");
  return text.includes("holds an entry with no version") || text.includes("holds a patch with no version string");
});
```
Keep the surrounding lines unchanged: the `assets`/`scripts` listing, the `expect(scripts.length).toBeGreaterThan(0)` guard, and `expect(readers).toEqual([])`. Do not touch `entryAndPreloads()`, `probes()`, or the other two `it` blocks.

## Tests

- `apps/web/src/net/first-load.test.ts`, existing test `#3499 no built script ...` (renamed per step 1): asserts no file in `dist/assets/*.js` contains either probe string. Passes on a correct bundle; fails if the worker inlines either `patch-meta.ts` or `patch-meta.browser.ts`.
- No new test file or new test case is needed: the fix extends the existing guard's probe set, and the issue asks only for that.
- Commands, in order (the `describe.skipIf(!existsSync(BUILT))` block skips without a bundle, so build first):
  - `pnpm --dir apps/web build`
  - `pnpm --dir apps/web test src/net/first-load.test.ts`
- Sanity check the negative direction once: temporarily remove `patchMeta()` from the worker `plugins` in a scratch copy (do not commit it), rebuild, and confirm the worker test fails on the `holds a patch with no version string` probe; then restore and rebuild.

## Done when

- [ ] The worker test flags both `holds an entry with no version` and `holds a patch with no version string`, with its comment naming `patch-meta.ts` and `patch-meta.browser.ts`.
- [ ] `pnpm --dir apps/web build` then `pnpm --dir apps/web test src/net/first-load.test.ts` is green with the target test actually run, not skipped (confirm `dist/` exists first).
- [ ] No test skipped, ignored, weakened, or deleted; no lint suppression, timeout raise, or unrelated reformat.

## Risks

- False positive from the new probe: avoided because `holds a patch with no version string` occurs only in `patch-meta.browser.ts` (verified by search); `holds no patches` was rejected as a probe because it occurs in both files.
- Guard silently skipping: the `dist`-gated `describe` skips without a build, so the builder must build before running the test and must check the test ran.
- Scope creep into the plugin or aliases: the builder changes only the test's title, comment, and filter, leaving resolution behavior as #3682 left it.

## Open questions

- None.
